causes: Habeas Corpus — Immediate and Unconditional Discharge from Parole (Pen. Code §1473)
CDCR Policy 19-03 is an invalid underground regulation (Gov. Code §11342.600; Tidewater Marine v. Bradshaw) and exceeds statutory authority under PC §3008(d)(2)
Use of obsolete Form 1502-DR instead of mandated Form 3043 violates 15 CCR §3574(f) (Accardi doctrine)
Substantive Due Process — no individualized finding of current dangerousness (In re Lawrence; In re Taylor)
Procedural Due Process — no notice, no hearing, no neutral decision-maker, no CTM meeting
key_facts: Petitioner (CDC No. BF3571) has been on parole since Dec. 2, 2020 following a 6-year term for PC §§289(a)(1)(A), 220(a)(1); registerable offense carries a 10-year statutory parole maximum (controlling discharge date Dec. 2, 2030) but Petitioner seeks earned discharge under PC §3008(d)(2)/15 CCR §3574. Over 5 years on parole: zero revocations, zero new arrests/offenses, CSRA score 2 (low risk), LS/CMI score 5 (Level 2 Below Average Risk — less than half the §3574(f)(1) retention threshold of 11), Stable-2007 score 6. Only incidents were four minor 2025 technical violations (missed HOPE sessions, uncharged GPS device), all resolved by verbal reprimand or PACT referral, never revocation. On Dec. 1, 2025, CDCR conducted a discharge review: Agent Long Moua recommended 'Retain on Parole'; Unit Supervisor Gary Noguchi and Parole Administrator Keely Dodd concurred, citing (a) Policy 19-03's 6.5-year 'time-served' minimum (only ~4 of 6.5 years served), (b) 'incomplete treatment' under HOPE, (c) the technical violations, and (d) unemployment — the last two years of which was itself state-induced: Parole Agent Derrick and HOPE Director Katie Palacios denied a scheduling accommodation for a March 2025 FedEx Office offer ($20/hr), forcing Petitioner's resignation around April 17, 2025, after which the Department cited the resulting joblessness as an aggravating factor. Petitioner argues Policy 19-03 is an unadopted 'underground regulation' that impermissibly converts §3008(d)(2)'s discretionary 'up to' the entire parole term into a mandatory 6.5-year minimum (In re Gadlin (2020) 10 Cal.5th 915; In re Leman (2021) 66 Cal.App.5th 200), and that CDCR used the obsolete Form 1502-DR instead of the Form 3043 mandated by 15 CCR §3574(f) (effective April 17, 2025), bypassing objective actuarial thresholds and the requirement that treatment status be decoupled from discharge eligibility (§3574(e)). Discloses (per Cal. Rules of Court, rule 4.552) a prior, factually distinct habeas petition filed in this Court in April/May 2025 (three-year vs. ten-year parole-term issue), denied by Judge Geffon on August 27, 2025 — not a bar to this petition under the successive-petition doctrine (In re Clark (1993) 5 Cal.4th 750) because it raises new claims based on the Dec. 1, 2025 denial and the newly effective §3574. Government Tort Claim presented Feb. 10, 2026, preserving damages arising from the unlawful restraint. Companion to Matters 9, 10, 11, and 15, which arise from the same administrative record — as of July 24, 2026, all four have closed (Matter 9 demurrer sustained; Matter 10 denied without prejudice; Matter 11 dismissed with prejudice; Matter 15 dismissed with prejudice for safety reasons), making this the sole surviving vehicle for the entire Nov./Dec. 2025 discharge-review challenge. This matter's pending ruling (due by Aug. 1, 2026 per the Order Extending Time) now carries the full weight of that challenge alone.
procedural_status: Petition signed and dated March 31, 2026; filed April 3, 2026, Santa Clara Superior Court (venue proper — Petitioner's underlying 2018 conviction and commitment originated there; Trial Ct. No. C1761642). Case number assigned: C2604791. July 2, 2026: Hon. Robert Hawk issued Order Extending Time — court must extend the time in which to rule because of need to thoroughly review voluminous papers and court's recent workload; time extended to August 1, 2026 (Cal. Rules of Court, rule 4.551(i)); cc: Petitioner, District Attorney (motions_dropbox@dao.sccgov.org), Research (4-1F). Notably, this order was filed the same day CDCR effected the retaliatory inter-county parole transfer of Petitioner's supervision to Santa Clara County (Matter 3/15) — the court's issuance of a formal Order Extending Time (rather than summary denial) signals the petition is being taken seriously. No separate Order to Show Cause issued by the earlier-anticipated June 5, 2026 date; the matter proceeded directly to the July 2, 2026 Order Extending Time, which governed the ruling deadline (August 1, 2026). AUGUST 1, 2026 RULING DEADLINE LAPSED WITHOUT A RULING: as of August 7, 2026, Judge Hawk has not ruled on the petition, and no further Order Extending Time or other communication has been received since the July 2, 2026 order. The petition remains pending and under submission; nothing in the record indicates denial, dismissal, or issuance of an Order to Show Cause. The lapse is recorded here as a fact of the docket posture — Petitioner has not yet made any inquiry to the court or sought relief arising from the delay. Exhibits: (A) CDCR Discharge Review Report/Form 1502-DR (Dec. 1, 2025); (B) In re Dwyer, San Mateo Super. Ct. No. SC-080355A/HC-3020 (Mar. 20, 2023); (C) 15 CCR §3574 incl. Form 3043; (D) Centerline Wage Reference; (E) FedEx Office employment documentation; (F) Alliance for Constitutional Sex Offense Laws v. Macomber (Sacramento Super. Ct. No. 23STCP02378). Prayer for relief seeks discharge effective Dec. 2, 2025 (or the date of the Court's order), plus a declaration invalidating Policy 19-03 and voiding the Dec. 1, 2025 determination for use of the obsolete Form 1502-DR. Companion to Matter 10 (C2602632), which targets treatment compulsion; this petition targets the parole term itself and seeks immediate unconditional discharge.
damages: Equitable: Immediate unconditional discharge from parole, effective Dec. 2, 2025. Government Tort Claim presented Feb. 10, 2026 preserves a separate damages track for the unlawful restraint.
